workPackages.title: Work package — the LC-MS/MS proteomics characterization was performed on a representative commercial-scale batch or a labora…
items: Amendment: Add an explicit statement in the identity and composition section clarifying whether the LC-MS/MS proteomics analysis reported in Table 11 was performed on material drawn from one or more of the five commercial-scale lots documented in Table 3 (five-batch analysis) or from a separate laboratory preparation. If the proteomics was performed on commercial-scale material, state the lot identifier(s) and confirm that the material met the food-grade specifications in Table 2. If the proteomics was performed on a laboratory preparation, add a bridging statement explaining how that preparation is representative of commercial-scale product in terms of protein concentration, processing steps applied, and any relevant compositional parameters.

Research/verification: Verify internal production and analytical records to confirm the source and scale of the material used for LC-MS/MS proteomics. If records confirm commercial-scale origin, compile the lot identification and batch records and incorporate them into the filing. If records indicate a laboratory preparation was used, assess whether any of the five commercial-scale lots in Table 3 can be re-analyzed by LC-MS/MS to confirm proteomics representativeness; if re-analysis is not feasible, document the comparability of the laboratory preparation to commercial-scale material using existing compositional data.

citations.excerpt: LLP is standardized to not less than 80% protein on an 'as is' basis. The other major components are ash and dietary fiber, and a small amount of fat.
Plantible's Lemna protein product is a highly purified protein product containing a minimum of 80% protein, of which >70% is Rubisco protein as confirmed through SDS PAGE analysis.

deliverables: Lot identification and batch records for the material used in LC-MS/MS proteomics analysis
Confirmation that the proteomics material met food-grade specifications in Table 2 or a documented comparison to commercial-scale lots in Table 3
If a laboratory preparation was used, a compositional comparison to commercial-scale lots demonstrating representativeness

workPackages.title: Work package — the purification process (activated carbon, ultrafiltration) could concentrate or generate novel bioactive co…
items: Amendment: Add a dedicated section or subsection in the manufacturing and compositional characterization portions of the filing that explicitly addresses the potential for the activated carbon and ultrafiltration purification steps to concentrate pre-existing bioactive components or generate novel process-related impurities. This section should identify the classes of compounds that could be affected by each purification step based on the known chemistry of those processes, compare the levels of relevant compounds in LLP to those in the unpurified Lemna minor plant material and in Mankai where data are available in the filing, and explain why the documented compositional profile of LLP—including the anti-nutrient and contaminant data in Table 18 and the proteomics data in Table 11—demonstrates that no novel bioactive components of concern are present at levels not accounted for in the safety assessment.

Research/verification: Review existing internal process development records and any available analytical data comparing LLP at intermediate purification stages (pre- and post-activated carbon; pre- and post-ultrafiltration) to the final product to determine whether any compounds are concentrated or depleted by those steps. If such records exist, compile the relevant data and incorporate a summary into the filing. If intermediate-stage analytical data are not available, assess whether the existing final-product compositional data in Table 18 and Appendix 2, combined with published literature on the chemistry of activated carbon adsorption and ultrafiltration of plant protein extracts, are sufficient to support a written argument that no novel bioactive components of concern are generated or concentrated by the purification process.

citations.excerpt: the chemical composition of duckweeds is not meaningfully different between species. Differences seen in macro nutrient profile (i.e., ratio of protein to starch) and mineral content are not species dependent but rather differ by the production process and nutrients available in the water.
Given the similarity in the composition of duckweeds and more purified products, it is reasonable to assume that LLP is also not genotoxic.

deliverables: Analytical data or process development records comparing LLP composition at intermediate purification stages to the final product, or a documented rationale for why such data are not necessary

A written assessment identifying the classes of compounds affected by activated carbon adsorption and ultrafiltration in the context of Lemna minor protein extraction and explaining why the final-product compositional data in the filing bound any process-related impurity concerns
Confirmation that the anti-nutrient and contaminant data in Table 18 cover the compound classes most likely to be concentrated by the purification steps

workPackages.title: Work package — the proteomics characterization is representative of commercial-scale production
items: Amendment: Add an explicit statement identifying the production scale and lot number of the material used for LC-MS/MS proteomics, cross-reference that lot to the representative commercial batch records, and explain any differences between the analyzed preparation and routine commercial production.

Research/verification: Verify existing production and analytical records for the proteomics sample. If those records establish commercial-scale provenance, compile a signed lot-traceability memorandum and supporting batch comparison. If the sample was a laboratory preparation, assess existing comparative data before deciding whether one commercial-lot proteomics analysis is needed.

citations.excerpt: the chemical composition of duckweeds is not meaningfully different between species. Differences seen in macro nutrient profile (i.e., ratio of protein to starch) and mineral content are not species dependent but rather differ by the production process and nutrients available in the water.
Given the similarity in the composition of duckweeds and more purified products, it is reasonable to assume that LLP is also not genotoxic.

deliverables: Proteomics sample lot identifier and chain-of-custody record
Comparison of the analyzed lot with representative commercial batches

workPackages.title: Work package — the 100% market penetration assumption adequately bounds upper-tail exposure for ages 1-3 for copper given ab…
items: Amendment: Revise the dietary exposure and risk assessment sections to explicitly address the availability and adequacy of WWEIA 2021–2023 data for the ages 1–3 subgroup. If WWEIA data for ages 1–3 are available and were used, state this explicitly and confirm that the 100% market penetration assumption was applied to that age group in the copper exposure calculation. If WWEIA data for ages 1–3 are absent or insufficient, add a transparent explanation of how upper-tail copper exposure for that age group was bounded, including any conservative assumptions applied as a substitute, and explain why those assumptions are adequate given the copper levels documented in the filing and the exclusion of toddler-specific food categories stated on page 37.

Research/verification: Review the WWEIA 2021–2023 dataset to determine whether consumption data for ages 1–3 are available for the food categories listed in Table 19. If data are available, verify that they were incorporated into Table 20 and Appendix 5. If data are absent for that age group, compile the existing copper content data from the filing's compositional tables and the exclusion criteria on page 37 to construct a written bounding argument demonstrating that the combination of category exclusions and the 100% market penetration assumption at maximum inclusion rates is sufficient to bound upper-tail copper exposure for ages 1–3 without requiring new dietary survey data.

citations.excerpt: For the 2+ age group, the 90th percentile consumption by users is 15.8 g/day or 0.282 g/kg bw/day. The highest intake on a body weight basis is for ages 4-8, which was 0.719 g/kg bw/day.

Foods that are consumed by infants and toddlers, such as infant formulas or foods formulated for babies or toddlers, and meat and poultry products that come under USDA jurisdiction are excluded from the list of intended food uses

deliverables: Confirmation of whether WWEIA 2021–2023 includes consumption data for ages 1–3 for the relevant food categories in Table 19
If ages 1–3 WWEIA data are absent, a documented bounding argument using existing copper content data and category exclusion criteria from the filing
Explicit copper exposure estimate or upper bound for ages 1–3 derived from available data and stated assumptions

workPackages.title: Work package — the expert panel's reliance on GRN 742's regulatory outcome as a confidence anchor constitutes an independent…
items: Amendment: Revise the expert panel consensus statement to reframe the panel's conclusion as an independent scientific evaluation of LLP's own compositional data, safety evidence, and exposure assessment, rather than as a conclusion 'largely based on substantial equivalence to LENTEIN Complete.' The revised statement should describe the specific evidence the panel independently evaluated—including the compositional analyses, proteomics data, anti-nutrient levels, and exposure calculations documented in the filing—and state the panel's conclusion in terms of that evidence. References to GRN 742 and its underlying data may be retained as supporting context where the panel independently assessed the relevance and adequacy of that data, but the GRN 742 'No Objections' letter should not be presented as a confidence anchor or as a basis for the panel's conclusion. The revised language should reflect that each panelist individually and collectively critically reviewed the evidence pertinent to LLP specifically.

Research/verification: Compile the specific evidence elements that the expert panel reviewed in forming its conclusion—including the compositional tables, proteomics results, exposure calculations, and toxicology narrative in the filing—and verify that each element is explicitly referenced in the revised expert panel statement as a basis for the panel's independent conclusion. No new studies are needed; the task is to verify that the existing evidence base is accurately and completely described in the expert panel statement as the foundation for an independent conclusion.

citations.excerpt: The evaluation of LLP is largely based on its substantial equivalence to LENTEIN TM Complete, described in GRN 742. FDA issued a "No Objections" letter to GRN 742 on August 22, 2018.
This GRAS conclusion for LLP is based on scientific procedures in accordance with 21 CFR 170.30(a) and 170.30(b).

deliverables: Revised expert panel consensus statement language that identifies the specific LLP-specific evidence reviewed and states an independent conclusion based on that evidence
Confirmation that each panelist's independent review of LLP-specific evidence is documented in the statement
Removal or recontextualization of the GRN 742 'No Objections' letter as a confidence anchor in the expert panel statement
